key_insight: Low-dimensional capping makes 3D perovskite surfaces rougher while improving photoluminescence and preserving electronic uniformity, even during accelerated aging.
engineering_relevance: Surface smoothness alone may be a poor screening metric for durable perovskite photovoltaics; electronic uniformity should also guide interface design.
method: Form mixed-dimensional heterostructures using 5-tert-butyl-phenanthridinium-derived Ruddlesden–Popper capping layers.
Compare statistical AFM topography with confocal, spatially resolved photoluminescence and quasi-Fermi level splitting.
Evaluate pristine and capped films under accelerated aging.
evidence_signal: Despite increased roughness and height asymmetry, capped films show enhanced photoluminescence, reduced non-radiative recombination, and more spatially uniform radiative quasi-Fermi level splitting than pristine films.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative effect sizes, aging conditions, or device-level efficiency and lifetime results.
paper_title: Electronic-morphological decoupling in mixed-dimensional halide perovskite heterostructures
